highlights.title: It’s the year of smartphone price hikes
highlights.summary: Paying more for a new phone seems almost unavoidable after Apple's event today. The new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max start at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively - a $100 price hike over their predecessors.
body: Apple, Google, and Samsung’s new phones have two things in common: they include a foldable and they cost more.

Google and Samsung followed the same formula as Apple when they each launched new phones over the past few months. The Pixel 11 starts at $899, up from $799 for last year’s Pixel 10. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra launched at $2,099, $100 more than the Galaxy Z Fold 7 it replaced.

You could try looking for a phone from a brand outside the big three, but the price hikes persist there, too. Sony’s new Xperia 10 VIII costs £150 more, and this year’s Moto Razr phones also cost $100 more than their predecessors, each offering little to no significant upgrades to go with their higher prices. Smartphone sales data shows that the market for phones under $100 may be on its way to completely disappearing.

highlights.title: MIT Schwarzman College of Computing launches pilot to help educators teach AI across disciplines
highlights.summary: A weeklong summer workshop brought higher education faculty to campus to explore how AI and machine learning materials can be adapted for their classrooms.
body: “The broader goal is to expand AI education to more students by investing in training for instructors,” says Dan Huttenlocher, dean of the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing and the Panasonic Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS).

“We want to empower students to become critical thinkers about AI, not just users of the technology,” says Asu Ozdaglar, deputy dean of academics for the MIT Schwarzman College and department head of EECS.

Bringing the program to life required broad collaboration across the college, including support from leadership, staff, and contributions from more than half a dozen instructors in fields ranging from finance and computer science to sustainability. Together, they helped shape a workshop that paired core technical concepts with examples and teaching materials adaptable to a range of classroom settings.

highlights.title: Chelsea hit SIX second-half goals to see off Leeds in Carabao Cup classic
highlights.summary: An incredible second-half comeback including six goals in 41 minutes saw Chelsea finally blow away Leeds 6-3 in one of the all-time Carabao Cup classics at Stamford Bridge.
body: The Blues found themselves two goals behind when Brendon Aaronson struck after 47 minutes to add to Tarik Muharemovic's opener and it appeared Xabi Alonso's first real cup test would end in disappointment - despite the half-time introduction of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Reece James.

But a Rogers-inspired comeback, with the England winger making four of their six subsequent goals, saw Chelsea net three times in seven minutes to lead before Danny Welbeck added a fourth to give them breathing space by firing through Michael Zetterer's legs.

Not for the first time in Alonso's short reign however, chaos once again reigned over control as Leeds continued to create chances before Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled them back to within a goal with 15 minutes to go.

It was still uncertain that Chelsea had finally sealed their progress when Barco blasted them 5-3 up from close range from another Rogers assist, but they could finally rest easy in added time - and extinguish Leeds' commendable never-say-die attitude - when Welbeck nodded Barco's wildly mishit effort beyond Zetterer.

highlights.title: Xbox Gets Exclusive Call of Duty Gun Skin PlayStation Players Can't See
highlights.summary: The console war has found a new battlefield, and this time it’s the latest Call of Duty entry. Xbox players are getting a special Modern Warfare 4 gun skin that PlayStation and PC players literally cannot see.
body: Activision just announced the “Inner Circuit” M4 blueprint as a bonus for anyone who digitally pre-orders Modern Warfare 4.
While everyone gets the same weapon blueprint with identical stats, Xbox players get a very different-looking version.

The Xbox-exclusive treatment celebrates the console’s 25th anniversary with a translucent green design inspired by the original Xbox, complete with Xbox branding on the magazine. On Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Windows PC, the same weapon instead has a more traditional mil-spec appearance.
A console-exclusive skin on its own isn't odd, but here's where things get weird: The Xbox version isn't visible to anyone playing on another platform.

body: Note that these estimates are based on gross revenue from player spending across the App Store and Google Play only. It does not feature estimates from alternative marketplaces or direct-to-consumer platforms.

Aniplex’s long-running gacha Fate/Grand Order has seen player spending spike to its highest monthly sum of the year. The game made $57.7 million this August with an anniversary celebration in Japan, more than doubling July’s $22.5m.

In fact, this was the anime-style RPG’s best month since last August. The game makes 89% of its earnings from Japan, meaning the month is a major one each year - more than the North American anniversary in early July.

On a daily spending basis, earnings reached their highest in more than five years this August. Fate/Grand Order generated $4.6m on the 15th, surpassing any daily record from the past five anniversaries but not quite matching the game’s lifetime high of $5.6m on January 1st, 2021.

highlights.title: Your Favorite Hollywood Hotspot? Guess Who Owns It.
highlights.summary: A billionaire Abu Dhabi royal has been snapping up Hollywood watering holes like they’re going out of style. But two LA hangouts – the Sunset Tower and the San Vicente Bungalows – just turned down a $700M offer.
body: What do Annabel’s, Sexy Fish, Delilah and the Bird Streets Club have in common — besides serving as Leonardo DiCaprio’s natural habitat? They’re all now controlled by investment interests tied to Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the Abu Dhabi royal who has been snapping up trophy properties across L.A. — and whose acquisition spree recently sparked rumors up and down the strip that the Sunset Tower Hotel and Jeff Klein’s San Vicente clubs might be next.

Tahnoon isn’t merely some fabulously rich dude who woke up one morning with a taste for bottle service. In addition to assembling a sizable collection of the world’s most celebrity-clogged watering holes, he happens to be the UAE president’s brother, the country’s national security adviser and deputy ruler of Abu Dhabi. His investment universe extends well beyond IHC: He also chairs the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and AI giant G42.

But the sheikh must really love a red velvet rope because apparently his nightlife shopping spree isn’t over. According to a source familiar with the discussions, DIAFA recently approached Klein about buying the Sunset Tower and his San Vicente clubs for the princely sum of $700 million.

highlights.title: Suno releases its first AI music model made with record industry help
highlights.summary: Suno's new v6 AI music model is its first made with support from the record industry. Suno's Jack Brody told The Verge that v6 was "trained from the ground up, with a new set of data that does not include the same data that our previous models were trained on." The data includes content licensed…
body: One of the big changes in v6 is that there are actually three different models: v6, v6-wild, and v6-mini. Mini is the model available for free to all. It’s focused on fast, resource-light creation. The results it spits out are simpler and often have more artifacts that betray it as the product of an AI prompt. v6-wild is supposed to be more unpredictable. Brody said that v6-wild is designed for “happy accidents and natural imperfections.” Though, in my limited testing, I found it hard to notice a difference between wild and bog-standard v6.

All three models are dramatically better at understanding genre. I recycled a handful of prompts that I used with older models calling for “hyperpop” or “krautrock” songs that missed the mark by a mile. v6, on the other hand, nailed all the superficial hallmarks of any genre I threw at it.

highlights.title: I Let an AI Agent Hack All My Gadgets—and I’d Do It Again
highlights.summary: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC. But it also told me how to make everything a lot more secure.
body: You’re probably aware that frontier AI models have attained advanced cybersecurity capabilities in recent months. They can find zero-day bugs in large codebases and scan computers for vulnerabilities at lightning speed. To make things even more exciting, cybersecurity agents sometimes go rogue, colluding with one another and hacking into outside systems to gain an edge.

But Will, you might be thinking, giving an impish, all-powerful cybersecurity agent access to your home network is batshit. And you would be correct! Nevertheless, I believe that a good way to understand the cybersecurity hellscape in front of us is to pay it a visit.
I got the idea for the experiment after discovering Abliteration AI, a startup that offers access to powerful AI models with the usual guardrails removed.

Most mainstream AI models will refuse to respond to certain queries, and they will certainly refuse to find and exploit vulnerabilities in computer systems. But it’s possible to remove these restrictions by finding and modifying certain patterns within an open-weight model’s internal parameters. You can tweak the patterns that lead to refusals through a process known as abliteration.
points: After I removed the safety guardrails from a powerful open-source model, it found vulnerabilities in my household devices and hacked into a PC.
But it also told me how to make everything a lot more secure.

highlights.title: Gauff to face new world No 1 Rybakina in semis after incredible comeback
highlights.summary: Coco Gauff saved two match points on her way to a three-set victory over teenage French Open winner Mirra Andreeva which set up a semi-final showdown with newly-crowned world No 1 Elena Rybakina.
body: It was a horrible start for 2023 champion Gauff, whose serve and forehand deserted her as she lost the first set in just 26 minutes, hitting only three winners and making 14 unforced errors.
She improved in the second which culminated in a tie-break, during which Russian fifth seed Andreeva squandered two chances to take the match.
That broke Andreeva's spirit and she risked being defaulted after hurling her racket towards her chair, inadvertently sending it spinning towards a camera operator who had to dodge out of the way.
Gauff eventually won 2-6 7-6 (7) 6-2 and revealed she took inspiration from a fellow American's comeback on Tuesday.

highlights.title: Michael Mann Recuts Miami Vice for October Beyond Fest World Premiere
highlights.summary: Writer-director Michael Mann is taking another crack at his 2006 film, Miami Vice. It was announced today that Miami Vice: Director’s Final Cut will make its world premiere at Beyond Fest in Los Angeles on October 3, 2026, followed by a Q&A with Mann.
body: It is described as “Michael Mann’s new cut” and that it will be shown in 4K. The Beyond Fest site doesn’t list the running time of this new cut.

If this version is truly a “new cut" then it will be an even different version of the film than the Miami Vice: Unrated Director’s Edition that was released on Blu-ray in 2008. The Unrated Director’s Edition is a re-edited film featuring scenes that were cut from the theatrical release as well as new music cues.

“These changes are enough to make this Miami Vice a slightly different and in some ways better experience than the theatrical cut, although the film's same fundamental flaws remain,” as I wrote in my review of the Unrated Director’s Edition at the time.

“This edition, however, is closer in tone to the TV series [which Mann exec produced but did not create], enough to have muted some of that criticism. For example, it opens with an offshore speedboat race set against the sunny Miami skyline and scored with electronic music, which conjures memories of the series' opening credits.”

body: Taking place on September 14th, 2026 in Bratislava, PixelCon is a free, open conference aimed at game developers, students, indie creators and professionals from across the games industry. Registration is required due to limited capacity.

Among the international speakers is Jeremy Widdowson, head of growth at Rovio, bringing experience from one of Europe's best-known mobile games companies, the studio behind the global Angry Birds franchise.

The programme also features Stanislav Stankovič, game design director at Electronic Arts, Maya Hofree, general manager of Hay Day at Supercell, and Florian Blaesche, director of player experience at Wooga, who will share their perspectives on building successful mobile games, player engagement and long-term retention.
The international line-up will be joined by Slovak and Czech industry leaders, including Pixel Federation experts and founders of local studios such as Flyboys, PowerPlay Studio and Impact Games.

highlights.title: ‘Entourage’ Creator Slams ‘God-Awful’ Ad Reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier: A ‘S—ty Imitation’ That ‘Makes Me Puke’
highlights.summary: “Entourage” creator Doug Ellin has spoken out against an ad reuniting Jeremy Piven and Adrian Grenier, calling it a “cheap, shitty imitation” of his beloved HBO comedy.
body: On Wednesday, Variety broke the news of Piven and Grenier’s on-screen reunion, which took place in a three-minute spot for Jake Paul’s gambling app Betr. Ellin said in a video message that he received “400 messages” about the “god-awful commercial,” clarifying that he was not involved in its creation.

Ellin said he’s not bitter over not being paid for the ad. He simply wishes the writers of “Entourage” would get more credit for the hard work they put into the scripts and character development, only for their work to be distilled into an “embarrassing” emulation of the HBO hit.

“I watch it and I want to throw up, because I would suffer, along with many other people, over every syllable, every fucking word,” Ellin said. “So I watch this trash, this shit, and go, ‘Ugh, ugh.’ There’s no bitterness. I want everyone to get paid, get rich. Just fucking do your own shit. That’s all.”

Ellin then seemed to take a shot at Piven — who won three Emmys for playing Ari on the series — claiming that the actor distanced himself from “Entourage” in the years following the 2011 series finale and 2015 movie.

highlights.title: San Francisco Orders Meta to Stop ‘Allowing’ AI Child Abuse Ads
highlights.summary: The City Attorney’s Office has asked Meta to explain how the harmful ads repeatedly ran on Facebook and Instagram. The company claims the ads are not under the city’s jurisdiction.
body: On Tuesday, WIRED reported that Meta has run more than 350 ads in recent months that transformed still images of minors—some of them confirmed as real individuals, including a member of a European royal family —into short videoclips that can depict them performing sexual acts. When clicked, these ads would direct people to download AI image- and video-generation apps, some of which could be used to digitally undress people or create other nonconsensual intimate imagery.

The ads, which were discovered by researchers at the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), included some identical ads that had been uploaded multiple times, and in total they reached more than 29,000 accounts in countries in the European Union. The ads that were shown across Facebook, Instagram, and Threads also targeted accounts in the US, Australia, and India. WIRED initially reported on a batch of 53 of the ads at the start of August, but more than 250 of the total number of ads ran on Meta’s platforms after this initial report.

highlights.title: Microsoft has new AI privacy rules for schools
highlights.summary: Microsoft agreed to a set of safety and privacy principles for AI in schools a week after two major school systems announced a ban on student-facing AI. In a new agreement with the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), the second-largest teachers union in the US, and its New York City affiliate…
body: Amid a policy crackdown, it’s agreeing to avoid training on student data and prohibit AI companions.

The agreement comes after New York City and Los Angeles both implemented one-year bans on AI tools for many students, giving the districts time to consider the proper use and guardrails. As parents and some educators have resisted the use of AI and screens more generally in schools, Microsoft likely recognizes that similar decisions could be coming. Beginning in November, school districts can opt to add the terms to new or existing agreements without having to renegotiate their entire contracts.

The AFT, for its part, has been critical of tech in schools, but also open to working with tech companies to prepare for the current AI wave. In a May speech, AFT President Randi Weingarten called for a ban on screens before third grade as well as “student-facing AI” before middle school. But the group also announced a $23 million AI training hub for educators funded by Anthropic, Microsoft, and OpenAI.
points: Microsoft agreed to a set of safety and privacy principles for AI in schools a week after two major school systems announced a ban on student-facing AI.

highlights.title: Mac Allister wins it for Liverpool against Atletico on Barcola's eventful full debut
highlights.summary: Alexis Mac Allister's superb strike saw Liverpool come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 at Anfield as Bradley Barcola went off with "cramp" on an eventful home debut.
body: Barcola was making his first start for Liverpool but felt his calf in the second half and the £123m signing was substituted having missed three good chances to mark the occasion with a goal. It did not impact the result thanks to Mac Allister's rocket.

Marcos Llorente had opened the scoring for the Spanish side with his fifth goal against Liverpool when put through well by Julian Alvarez on the Argentine forward's return to the starting line-up. But that man Dominik Szoboszlai levelled it up before the break.

Curiously, both Liverpool goals came in the immediate aftermath of Barcola chances. Jan Oblak saved to deny him in the build-up to Szoboszlai's goal, Ronald Araujo cleverly recycling the chance. And Mac Allister blasted in to spare his blushes for the second.

Liverpool had drawn their first two Premier League games of the season two apiece, and given the open nature of the game there was a risk of a repeat. But instead Andoni Iraola earned this Anfield victory in his first Champions League match as a head coach.

body: Judging from the substantial footage shown, Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is a 1:1 remake, aside from a visual overhaul and some smart additions, similar to Starfox from earlier this year. One of the additions I’m less excited about, though, is the introduction of a dedicated jump button that Ocarina of Time doesn’t need.

In Ocarina of Time on the Nintendo 64, Link negotiated his fair share of platforms. From the very start of the adventure, he jumped between ledges, such as the small islands in a pond in Kokiri Forest. However, the player didn’t control those hops. Instead, they directed Link to run toward the edge of a platform and then he would automatically take a wild leap from its edge, all on his own.

highlights.title: 4 groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
highlights.summary: A nearly identical exploit kit that targets critical vulnerabilities in both Chromium-based browsers and older versions of Windows is being actively used by at least four hacking groups, some of which have ties to the Chinese government.
body: Researchers from security firm Proofpoint said Wednesday that BlueMoon, the name they gave to the kit, chains three vulnerabilities together so the attackers using it can install malware of their choice. BlueMoon exploits two Chromium vulnerabilities and one in the kernel of Windows 10 (Oct 2018 Update), Windows Server 2019, Windows 10 2004, Windows Server 2022, and the initial release of Windows 11. All three vulnerabilities have received patches in the past 24 hours.

The attacks lacked the stealth found in many campaigns. More often, hackers want to exploit newly discovered vulnerabilities sparingly to lengthen their longevity. Proofpoint hypothesized that one reason for the widely used and visible exploit chain was to take advantage of a “patch gap” in the Chromium supply chain, which spans the time a patch is available from developers and the time that patch is incorporated into browsers such as Chrome and Edge. Another likely contributor was the use of AI, which can often spot vulnerabilities faster than discovery performed solely by humans.

body: We’re announcing the appointment of Paul Christiano to the OpenAI Foundation Board. He will be a non-voting observer on the OpenAI Group PBC Board.

Paul will also join the Safety and Security Committee (SSC) of the Foundation Board, working alongside its chair, Zico Kolter. The SSC provides governance over safety and security practices across all of OpenAI, including OpenAI Group PBC.

Paul brings government experience spanning two administrations through his work at the Center for AI Standards and Innovation ⁠ (opens in a new window) (CAISI) within the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), an agency of the U.S. Department of Commerce, where he is a Senior Tech Advisor 1. During his time at CAISI and its predecessor, the U.S. AI Safety Institute, Paul has worked on evaluating frontier AI models, including capabilities with national security implications, and on approaches to mitigating associated safety and security risks.

body: Also this week, that firm, The Exploration Company, announced a significant capital raise of $450 million in Series C funding. Although not spectacular by the standards of some US space businesses, this is the largest-ever Series C funding round by a Europe-based space company, and likely the largest funding round ever raised by a female-led company in Europe.

And Huby has arrived on center stage in the European space community at a time when there are increasingly urgent questions about the ability of the continent to navigate a future in space as commercial startups in the United States and China race ahead.

So many of the biggest European space projects of this decade feel dated. The flagship rocket, the Ariane 6 vehicle, is flying. But its costs are high, it is fully expendable, and its flight rate of 10 launches a year feels antediluvian in the megaconstellation era. Europe’s response to SpaceX’s Starlink constellation is a project called IRIS², which is already years behind schedule and has seen its estimated cost balloon to more than $15 billion before much metal has even been cut.

highlights.title: Massachusetts hits data centers with new clean power rules
highlights.summary: Massachusetts has become the third state in as many months to slap new restrictions on data center development.
body: Massachusetts became the latest state to force data centers to bring their own power, but this time there’s a twist. A new state mandate would require developers building data centers larger than 25 megawatts to provide clean power or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.

Gov. Maura Healey’s executive order is the latest example of states turning against data centers. Just a few years ago, tech companies and data center developers were showered with incentives to locate facilities in a particular state. Now, they’re fighting a groundswell of public opposition as politicians seek to show voters they’re addressing their concerns.

Under Healey’s order, data centers larger than 25 megawatts of peak demand will have to bring their own power and guarantee that it adheres to the state’s clean energy requirements. Healey would prefer that they generate the clean power onsite, too. If not, they’ll need to fund the construction of new generation nearby or pay into a ratepayer protection fund.

highlights.title: ‘I’m sick of her talking about it’: 11 readers share how GLP-1s have affected their relationships
highlights.summary: As weight loss drugs have risen all around the world, it has reshaped users’ relationships for better and for worse. As GLP-1 use continues to rise in the US and the UK, people’s bodies are being reshaped – as are their relationships.
body: “Relationships tend to develop a sense of equilibrium and predictability over time,” says Dr Lindsey Berisha, a licensed clinical psychologist who has worked with clients using GLP-1s for over 10 years. “When one partner undergoes a significant change, it can shift that equilibrium, and even positive change can create uncertainty for both partners.”

Berisha says that her clients who use GLP-1s often report feeling relieved that they are no longer consumed with thoughts of food. These users often develop more self-compassion, she says, as they realize what they previously interpreted as a failure or lack of self-control was a legitimate biological drive and food preoccupation that made life harder for them. “This shift can often be more impactful than the weight loss itself,” she says.

But these changes can elicit mixed reactions from partners, family and friends, says psychologist Dr Rachel Goldman, ranging “from being supportive to feeling insecure, left behind, or worried that the relationship itself is changing”.

highlights.summary: Apple says its new watches won’t save raw audio, but features that can transcribe recent speech and summarize ambient conversations raise new questions about consent, privacy, and how people behave when they know they could always be recorded.
body: Apple is trying to get consumers to accept, and even welcome, a new reality: Your tech is always listening.

At Wednesday’s “Surprise and Shine” iPhone event, where the company introduced its new hardware lineup, the real surprise turned out not to be the foldable iPhone, but how the famously privacy-sensitive tech giant has decided its watches will now be able to process live audio and transcribe what was said.
Does this mean you’re always being recorded if the person you’re interacting with is wearing an Apple Watch? Not exactly — though it may make some people uncomfortable regardless.

It also raises the question of whether consumers actually want this technology, or if Apple forged ahead in this area because it was afraid that another company, such as OpenAI, would soon introduce a competitive AI device of its own.

body: The entire Onimusha series takes place in an alternate version of Japan’s feudal era. In the game’s canon timeline, Way of the Sword picks up over two decades after the previous mainline release, Dawn of Dreams, bringing the world of Genma into the Edo period.

The companion webcomic, subtitled "Fated Rivalry," picks up pretty soon before the main events of Way of the Sword. The story follows Miyamoto Musashi's rival, Sasaki Ganryu, who discovers an Oni Gauntlet on his vengeance-driven quest to become powerful enough to take down Musashi.

The prequel is being produced by Laurel Pursuit, a US-based studio that’s previously distributed the Dungeon Crawler Carl graphic novel as well as original webcomics like Defiance of the Fall. The Ominusha webcomic specifically features work from Webtoon creators jjolee, hilluhri, and BAEKSSE.

The first chapter was released this past Saturday and has amassed just over 20,000 clicks so far. Future chapters will continue to become available on Saturdays, though it’s unclear how long the full prequel webcomic will end up being.

highlights.summary: There are four new moons left in 2026. Astrologist Lisa Stardust weighs in on how to harness the power of the new moon—along with practices to avoid.
body: This month’s new moon occurs at the beginning of the 29½-day lunar cycle, when the sun and the moon line up at the same degree and astrological sign in the sky. This partnership, which is called a “conjunction,” brings the sun's fiery exuberance and the moon's sentimentalism together. Since we can't see the moon’s glow on Earth, it is also known as a dark moon.

New moons are a time of transcendence, when the head and heart discuss how to move us forward to a better state of being. This is why we choose which aspirations to harness to put our dreams into motion for the next four weeks and eternity. Depending on the zodiac sign that the new moon falls in and the other astrological features at the time, we get refreshing guidance on what we should home in on.
The upcoming new moons of 2026 are September 10 in Virgo, October 10 in Libra, November 9 in Scorpio, and December 8 in Sagittarius. Here’s how to harness their energy.

The moon symbolizes the nostalgic part of our spirits, which is why looking back and learning from our past is essential at every lunar phase. As long as we are taking the time to understand how we can evolve and grow from these situations, we are on the right track.
